# Packin Club: full fact sheet

> Packin Club is a Delhi-based B2B manufacturer and supplier of certified compostable packaging for businesses across India. Founded in 2024. This file gives AI tools the key facts in one place. Short version: https://packinclub.com/llms.txt

## Company facts
- Name: Packin Club (also written PackinClub). Website: https://packinclub.com/
- Type: B2B manufacturer and supplier of compostable packaging
- Founded: 2024. The team started working on the idea in September 2022 and officially started operations in 2024.
- Location: D-1/64, 21st Century Business Centre, Veer Savarkar Block, Shakarpur, Nirman Vihar, Delhi 110092, India. Supplies businesses across India.
- Phone: +91 81784 14360. Email: info@packinclub.com
- Founder: Vikas Jha. Co-founder: Rajat Sharma
- Standards: IS 17088 (India's standard for compostable plastics), EN 13432, CPCB certified. Certificates are shared on request.
- Minimum order quantity: 100 kg per specification
- Samples and a quote: within two business days, via https://packinclub.com/contact.html
- Composting time (our specification): returns to soil within 240 days in industrial composting
- Sells to businesses only (B2B), not to individual consumers

## Home page FAQ
**What is compostable packaging?**
Compostable packaging is made from materials that break down into water, carbon dioxide and nutrient-rich humus under composting conditions, instead of fragmenting into microplastics. A genuine compostable claim needs certification, which in India means IS 17088. Read the full guide.

**Is compostable the same as biodegradable?**
No. “Biodegradable” has no fixed timeframe or test, so it is a broad marketing word. “Compostable” is a certified outcome with defined breakdown times and limits. Compostable vs biodegradable: the real difference.

**Which certifications do Packin Club products carry?**
Packin Club products are made to IS 17088, the Indian standard for compostable plastics, and are CPCB certified. Certificates are shared on request through the contact page. What IS 17088 means.

**How long does it take to compost?**
Our specification states that products return to soil within 240 days in industrial composting. They are designed for managed, industrial composting facilities, so the actual time depends on the temperature, moisture and conditions of the facility. How long does compostable packaging take to decompose?

**Which businesses and products do you supply?**
Packin Club supplies e-commerce and D2C brands, restaurants and cloud kitchens, retailers and supermarkets, farms and nurseries, hospitals, industrial and logistics teams, and temples. The range has 24 products, including courier mailers, carry bags, garbage bags, mulch film, pouches, cups, cling film and stretch film. See all products.

**What is the minimum order, and how do I get samples?**
The minimum order is 100 kg per specification. Tell us what you ship through the quote form and we send samples and a quote within two business days.

**Do you supply outside Delhi?**
Yes. Packin Club is based in Delhi and supplies businesses across India. Share your location and volumes when you request a quote so we can confirm delivery.

## About Packin Club: FAQ
**What is Packin Club?**
Packin Club is a Delhi-based B2B manufacturer and supplier of certified compostable packaging for businesses across India. Its mission is to take single-use plastic out of business and everyday life.

**When did Packin Club start?**
The team started working on the idea of Packin Club in September 2022, and the company officially started operations in 2024.

**Who founded Packin Club?**
Packin Club was founded by Vikas Jha, who leads strategy, partnerships and the Packin Club brand. Co-founder Rajat Sharma drives product, materials and the systems behind plastic-free manufacturing.

**Where is Packin Club based?**
Packin Club is based at D-1/64, 21st Century Business Centre, Veer Savarkar Block, Shakarpur, Nirman Vihar, Delhi 110092, and supplies businesses across India. You can reach the team on +91 81784 14360 or info@packinclub.com.

**What does Packin Club make and supply?**
Compostable bags, courier mailers, films, pouches, cups, mulch film, tissue and more: 24 formats for agriculture, retail, food service, healthcare, industrial and temple use. See all products.

**How can my business work with Packin Club?**
Tell us what you ship and your volumes through the contact page. We match each item to a certified compostable format, send samples for you to trial, and quote to your sizes and volumes within two business days.

## Products: FAQ
**How many products are there, and what categories?**
The range has 24 compostable packaging products in seven categories: Agriculture & Nursery, Bags on Roll, Healthcare & Hospital, HORECA, Industrial, Retail, and Temple & Religious. Use the Categories menu at the top of the page to filter.

**What is the minimum order quantity?**
The minimum order is 100 kg per specification. Share your size and thickness on the contact page and we will confirm what that means in units.

**Can I print my brand on the products?**
Printing is listed on each product page. For most products it is up to 8-colour flexographic printing with food-grade inks.

**Are the products certified?**
Packin Club products are made to IS 17088 and are CPCB certified. Certificates are shared on request. What IS 17088 means.

**How should I dispose of compostable packaging?**
Send it to industrial composting where available, and keep it out of plastic recycling. Our specification states that products return to soil within 240 days in industrial composting. Used medical waste bags are the exception: they follow your biomedical waste protocol. Home vs industrial composting.

**How do I choose the right size or thickness?**
Every product page has a sizes and thickness guide and its own FAQs. For courier bags, see the courier bag sizes chart. You can also send your product dimensions and we will suggest a size and send samples.

## Industries: FAQ
**Which industries do you supply?**
E-commerce and D2C, food service and HORECA, cloud kitchens and delivery, retail and fashion, grocery and supermarkets, agriculture and nursery, healthcare and hospitals, industrial and logistics, and temples and religious organisations.

**Can you match the plastic items I use today?**
Yes. We map each plastic item on your line by size, volume and function, pair it to a certified compostable format, or tool it to your exact spec where needed. Samples go out for you to test on your real packing lines before any commitment.

**What do restaurants and cloud kitchens use?**
Typical formats are hot liquid pouches rated up to 95°C, bread pouches, cling film, aqueous coated paper cups and bamboo tissue. Test any format against your menu and delivery routes before switching. Compostable packaging for restaurants and cloud kitchens.

**Do you supply packaging for healthcare?**
We supply colour-coded compostable bags for segregating non-hazardous clinical waste, made for BMWM 2016 colour segregation. Acceptance depends on your state pollution control board and treatment provider, so confirm your requirement first. Used bags containing biomedical waste follow your facility’s biomedical waste protocol and are not composted.

**What do farms and nurseries use?**
Compostable mulch film that is tilled into the soil at harvest, and nursery bags that are planted whole with the seedling. Compostable mulch film: a practical guide for Indian farmers.

**My industry is not listed. Can you still help?**
If you ship it, we can pack it. Tell us what you move and how, and we will match each format to a certified compostable equivalent or tool it to your exact spec. Start on the contact page.

## Products (24)

### Compostable Agri Mulch Film
Page: https://packinclub.com/products/compostable-agri-mulch-film.html
Category: Agriculture & Nursery

Summary: Suppresses weeds and holds soil moisture, then tills back into the earth, no retrieval, no residue.
Description: A field-grade biodegradable mulch film engineered to perform like conventional polyethylene mulch through a full growing season, then break down in situ. Lay it, plant through it, and till it back into the soil at harvest. There is nothing to lift, collect, or send to landfill, and no microplastic left in your field.

Key features:
- Suppresses weed growth without herbicides
- Retains soil moisture and stabilises root-zone temperature
- Tills directly into soil, zero retrieval labour
- Leaves no microplastic residue behind
- Available in black, clear, and silver-reflective finishes

Specifications:
- Thickness: 15 – 25 microns
- Roll width: 0.6 m – 2.0 m (made to bed size)
- Roll length: 400 m – 1000 m
- Field life: 3 – 6 months (formulated to crop cycle)
- Base material: Corn-starch + PLA + PBAT compostable blend
- Certification: IS 17088 · CPCB certified · EN 13432
- Compostability: Returns to soil within 240 days (industrial)
- Printing: Up to 8-colour flexographic, food-grade inks
- Shelf life: 12 months from date of manufacture
- Min. order qty: 100 kg per specification

Used for: Vegetable and row-crop beds; Strawberry and melon cultivation; Polyhouse and tunnel farming; Orchard and plantation ground cover

Who uses it: Compostable mulch film is bought by growers who want the weed control and moisture retention of plastic mulch without the cost of lifting and disposing of it at the end of the season. Typical users are vegetable and row-crop farms, strawberry and melon growers, polyhouse and tunnel operations, and orchards and plantations that use ground cover. Because the film is tilled into the soil at harvest instead of being collected, it suits farms where retrieval labour is expensive or where used plastic mulch is hard to clean and dispose of.

Sizing: Order the film width to match your bed: rolls run from 0.6 m to 2.0 m wide and from 400 m to 1000 m long, made to bed size. Longer rolls mean fewer changeovers on a mulch-laying machine, while shorter rolls are easier to handle by hand on small plots. Give us your bed width, row length and laying method when you request a quote.

How to choose thickness: Mulch film is made in 15 to 25 microns. Thinner film costs less per hectare and suits short crops and careful machine laying. Thicker film is more forgiving in wind and on rough soil, and is the safer choice for longer crops. The field life, from 3 to 6 months, is formulated to the crop cycle, so tell us your crop, planting date and expected harvest date. The film should last the crop but not far beyond it.

Disposal and storage: At the end of the crop, till the film into the soil instead of lifting it. Our specification states that the film returns to soil within 240 days in industrial composting. In the field the rate depends on soil temperature, moisture and microbial activity, so it will vary by region and season. Remove drip tape, clips and pegs before tilling. Store unused rolls in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight; shelf life is 12 months from the date of manufacture.

FAQ:
Q: What roll widths and lengths are available?
A: Widths run from 0.6 m to 2.0 m and lengths from 400 m to 1000 m. Widths are made to your bed size.
Q: How long does the film last in the field?
A: The field life is 3 to 6 months and is formulated to the crop cycle. Share your crop and planting window so the formulation can be matched.
Q: Do I need to remove the film at harvest?
A: No. The film is designed to be tilled directly into the soil, so there is nothing to lift or send to landfill. Remove non-compostable accessories such as drip tape first.
Q: Which colours are available?
A: Black, clear and silver-reflective finishes are available.
Q: What is the minimum order quantity?
A: The minimum order is 100 kg per specification. Share your roll width and length and we will confirm what that means in rolls.
Q: How do I get samples and a quote?
A: Use the quote form on this page or the contact page. Tell us your crop, bed width and planting date so we can suggest a thickness and roll size. We send samples and a quote within two business days.

### Compostable Nursery Bags
Page: https://packinclub.com/products/compostable-nursery-bags.html
Category: Agriculture & Nursery

Summary: Grow-bags that go straight into the ground at transplant, roots and all.
Description: Seedling and sapling grow-bags that you plant whole. The bag breaks down in the soil as the plant establishes, so roots are never disturbed at transplant and transplant shock is all but eliminated. A cleaner, faster alternative to single-use polythene nursery sleeves.

Key features:
- Plant the whole bag, no transplant shock
- Breaks down as roots establish
- Breathable walls promote healthy root structure
- Eliminates polythene waste at nurseries
- Punched drainage holes standard

Specifications:
- Sizes: 4"×6" to 10"×12" (custom on request)
- Thickness: 25 – 50 microns
- Gusset: Bottom-gusseted for fill stability
- Drainage: Pre-punched holes
- Base material: Corn-starch + PLA + PBAT compostable blend
- Certification: IS 17088 · CPCB certified · EN 13432
- Compostability: Returns to soil within 240 days (industrial)
- Printing: Up to 8-colour flexographic, food-grade inks
- Shelf life: 12 months from date of manufacture
- Min. order qty: 100 kg per specification

Used for: Forestry and reforestation saplings; Vegetable and flower seedlings; Retail nursery and garden centres; Horticulture and landscaping projects

Who uses it: Compostable nursery bags are used by forestry and reforestation programmes, vegetable and flower seedling growers, retail nurseries and garden centres, and horticulture and landscaping contractors. They suit any operation that raises seedlings or saplings in bags and wants to avoid stripping polythene sleeves at transplant. Because the whole bag is planted with the seedling, the roots are not disturbed at transplant and there is no polythene sleeve to collect afterwards. That helps most where large numbers of saplings are planted in the field and sleeve removal adds labour.

Sizing: Bags run from 4"×6" to 10"×12", with custom sizes on request. Choose by the root system at planting time: small seedlings and herbs suit the smaller sizes, while tree saplings that stay in the nursery for months need the larger ones. The bags are bottom-gusseted for fill stability and come with pre-punched drainage holes.

How to choose thickness: Nursery bags are made in 25 to 50 microns. A thinner wall breaks down sooner after planting and suits fast-growing seedlings that go into the ground quickly. A thicker wall holds its shape for longer, which suits saplings that stay in the nursery for several months or are moved by hand and truck. As a rule, match the wall to the time the plant spends in the bag: the longer the holding period, the thicker the film. Trial a small batch under your own watering and handling conditions before a full order.

Disposal and storage: Plant the bag together with the seedling. Our specification states that the bag returns to soil within 240 days in industrial composting. In the ground, breakdown depends on soil temperature, moisture and microbial activity. Cut off any plastic ties or labels before planting. Store unused bags in a cool, dry place; shelf life is 12 months from the date of manufacture.

FAQ:
Q: What sizes are the nursery bags?
A: Sizes run from 4"×6" to 10"×12". Custom sizes are available on request.
Q: Can the bag be planted with the seedling?
A: Yes. The bag is designed to be planted whole and to break down in the soil as the plant establishes, so the roots are not disturbed at transplant.
Q: Do the bags have drainage holes?
A: Yes. Drainage holes are pre-punched as standard, and the walls are breathable to support healthy root structure.
Q: Can I print my brand on it?
A: Yes. Printing is available in up to 8 colours using flexographic, food-grade inks. Many nurseries use print for the species name, brand or size.
Q: What is the minimum order quantity?
A: The minimum order is 100 kg per specification. Tell us your bag size and thickness and we will confirm the quantity this represents.
Q: How do I get samples and a quote?
A: Use the quote form on this page or the contact page. Share your bag size, how long plants stay in the bag, and your planting season. We send samples and a quote within two business days.

### Compostable Carry Bags on Roll
Page: https://packinclub.com/products/compostable-carry-bags-on-roll.html
Category: Bags on Roll

Summary: Perforated carry bags on a roll for fast, fuss-free dispensing at the till.
Description: Carry bags supplied on a perforated roll for high-throughput counters. Staff tear off one bag at a time with one hand, keeping queues moving while staying fully compliant with single-use-plastic bans. Mount on any standard roll dispenser.

Key features:
- One-handed tear-off dispensing
- Fits standard counter roll holders
- Consistent perforation, clean separation
- Compliant with single-use plastic bans
- Brandable with up to 8-colour print

Specifications:
- Bag size: 10"×14" to 16"×20"
- Bags per roll: 250 – 500
- Thickness: 20 – 40 microns
- Core: 1.5" cardboard core
- Base material: Corn-starch + PLA + PBAT compostable blend
- Certification: IS 17088 · CPCB certified · EN 13432
- Compostability: Returns to soil within 240 days (industrial)
- Printing: Up to 8-colour flexographic, food-grade inks
- Shelf life: 12 months from date of manufacture
- Min. order qty: 100 kg per specification

Used for: Supermarket and grocery checkouts; Produce and bakery sections; Pharmacy and convenience counters; Quick-service retail tills

Who uses it: Carry bags on a roll are used at counters where speed matters: supermarket and grocery checkouts, produce and bakery sections, pharmacy and convenience counters, and quick-service retail tills. Staff tear off one bag at a time with one hand, which keeps queues moving. The perforated roll mounts on a standard counter roll holder, so a store can switch from plastic rolls without buying new fixtures. Our specification lists the bags as compostable and compliant with single-use plastic bans.

Sizing: Bags run from 10"×14" to 16"×20", with 250 to 500 bags per roll on a 1.5" cardboard core. Choose by the typical purchase: smaller sizes suit pharmacy and bakery items, larger sizes suit grocery baskets. More bags per roll means fewer changeovers at a busy counter, but also a heavier roll, so check what your dispenser can carry.

How to choose thickness: Rolls are made in 20 to 40 microns. Lighter film suits light items such as bakery goods and pharmacy purchases. Heavier film is better for packaged groceries and items with corners. Thicker film is stronger but uses more material per bag, so choose the thinnest gauge that carries your typical load, and trial it at one counter before rolling out to every till.

Disposal and storage: Used bags should go to industrial composting where it is available, and not into plastic recycling. Our specification states that the bag returns to soil within 240 days in industrial composting. Bags used for food can go in with food waste. Keep unused rolls in a cool, dry place; shelf life is 12 months from the date of manufacture.

A: The rolls are made to fit standard counter roll holders. Send us your dispenser model or roll dimensions and we will check.
Q: Can staff tear off one bag at a time?
A: Yes. The roll is perforated for one-handed tear-off with clean separation.
Q: Can I print my brand on it?
A: Yes. Printing is available in up to 8 colours using flexographic, food-grade inks. Print your store name or message on every bag.

A: The minimum order is 100 kg per specification. Share your bag size and thickness and we will confirm the number of rolls.
Q: How do I get samples and a quote?

### Compostable Garbage Bag on Roll
Page: https://packinclub.com/products/compostable-garbage-bag-on-roll.html
Category: Bags on Roll

Summary: Leak-resistant bin liners on a roll for busy kitchens and facilities.
Description: Bin liners on a perforated roll for kitchens, offices, and facilities that get through a lot of them. Leak-resistant seams hold wet waste, and the whole liner composts with its contents in an industrial facility, no separating the bag from the food scraps.

Key features:
- Leak-resistant heat-sealed base
- Composts together with organic waste
- Perforated roll for quick replacement
- Sized to standard bins
- Available in multiple colours for waste segregation

Specifications:
- Bag size: 19"×21" to 30"×37"
- Bags per roll: 15 – 30
- Thickness: 30 – 51 microns
- Seal: Heat-sealed leak-resistant base
- Base material: Corn-starch + PLA + PBAT compostable blend
- Certification: IS 17088 · CPCB certified · EN 13432
- Compostability: Returns to soil within 240 days (industrial)
- Printing: Up to 8-colour flexographic, food-grade inks
- Shelf life: 12 months from date of manufacture
- Min. order qty: 100 kg per specification

Used for: Commercial and home kitchens; Offices and co-working spaces; Hotels and facility management; Municipal wet-waste collection

Who uses it: Bin liners on a roll are used where bags are changed many times a day: commercial and home kitchens, offices and co-working spaces, hotels and facility management teams, and municipal wet-waste collection. The perforated roll lets staff pull a fresh liner quickly. Because the liner composts together with organic waste in an industrial facility, kitchens and wet-waste collectors do not need to separate the bag from the food scraps. Several colours are available, which helps with waste segregation.

Sizing: Bags run from 19"×21" to 30"×37", with 15 to 30 bags per roll. Match the bag to the bin: measure the bin height and its circumference, and choose a bag long enough to fold over the rim. A bag that is too small slips into the bin, and one that is too large wastes material.

How to choose thickness: Liners are made in 30 to 51 microns. Light, dry waste such as office paper bins sits comfortably at the lower end. Wet kitchen waste and heavier loads suit the higher end, because the liner has to hold weight and resist tearing at the rim. The base is heat-sealed to resist leaks. If your team lifts full bags out by the top, choose the stronger gauge.

Disposal and storage: Compost the bag together with its contents in an industrial composting facility, and keep it out of the plastic recycling stream. Our specification states that the bag returns to soil within 240 days in industrial composting. Compostable liners are designed to degrade, so avoid leaving wet waste in a bag longer than necessary, especially in hot weather. Store unused rolls in a cool, dry place; shelf life is 12 months from the date of manufacture.

A: Sizes run from 19"×21" to 30"×37", with 15 to 30 bags per roll.

A: Yes. The base is heat-sealed to resist leaks, which suits wet kitchen waste.
Q: Can the liner be composted with food waste?
A: Yes. The liner composts together with organic waste in an industrial composting facility, so the waste does not need to be emptied out first.
Q: Can I get different colours for segregation?
A: Yes. Multiple colours are available to support waste segregation.
Q: What is the minimum order quantity?

### Compostable Medical Waste Bags
Page: https://packinclub.com/products/compostable-medical-waste-bags.html
Category: Healthcare & Hospital

Summary: Colour-coded, compliant bags for the safe handling of non-hazardous clinical waste.
Description: Colour-coded biomedical waste bags for the segregation and safe handling of non-hazardous clinical waste, made to a compostable specification. Strong seams and a high load rating meet the demands of hospital waste streams while reducing the plastic burden of healthcare facilities.

Key features:
- Colour-coded for BMWM segregation
- High puncture and tear resistance
- Leak-proof heat-sealed seams
- Printable with biohazard markings
- Compostable alternative to LDPE liners

Specifications:
- Colours: Yellow · Red · Blue (as per protocol)
- Sizes: 19"×21" to 33"×39"
- Thickness: 50 – 75 microns
- Compliance: Made for BMWM 2016 segregation
- Base material: Corn-starch + PLA + PBAT compostable blend
- Certification: IS 17088 · CPCB certified · EN 13432
- Compostability: Returns to soil within 240 days (industrial)
- Printing: Up to 8-colour flexographic, food-grade inks
- Shelf life: 12 months from date of manufacture
- Min. order qty: 100 kg per specification

Used for: Hospitals and nursing homes; Clinics and diagnostic labs; Pharmaceutical facilities; Veterinary practices

Who uses it: These bags are made for hospitals and nursing homes, clinics and diagnostic labs, pharmaceutical facilities and veterinary practices that segregate biomedical waste by colour. They are colour-coded, printable with biohazard markings, and made for BMWM 2016 segregation. They are a compostable-film alternative to LDPE liners for the segregation step. Before switching, check that the specification meets the requirements of your state pollution control board and your biomedical waste treatment provider.

Sizing: Bags run from 19"×21" to 33"×39". Choose the size from the bin or container the bag lines, and leave enough length to tie the neck securely. Colours are supplied as per your segregation protocol.

How to choose thickness: Medical waste bags are made in 50 to 75 microns. The lower end suits light dressings and soft waste. The higher end suits heavier loads and bags that are handled and moved often, because the film has to resist puncture and tearing. Sharps belong in rigid puncture-proof containers, not in bags. Seams are heat-sealed to prevent leaks.

Disposal and storage: Used bags that contain biomedical waste must be handled under your facility's biomedical waste protocol and sent to an authorised treatment facility. They are not for ordinary composting. Store unused bags in a cool, dry place; shelf life is 12 months from the date of manufacture.

FAQ:
Q: Which colours are available?
A: Yellow, red and blue, as per your segregation protocol.
Q: What sizes are available?
A: Sizes run from 19"×21" to 33"×39".
Q: Are the bags approved under the BMWM Rules 2016?
A: They are made for BMWM 2016 colour segregation, as stated in the specification. Acceptance depends on your state pollution control board and treatment provider, so confirm your requirement with them and share it with us when you request a quote.
Q: Can biohazard markings be printed on the bags?
A: Yes. The bags can be printed with biohazard markings, using up to 8-colour flexographic printing.
Q: What is the minimum order quantity?

If you use plastic poly mailers today, this is a compostable replacement in the same opaque, water-resistant format.

Sizing: Measure your packed item at its widest and tallest points, then choose a mailer with enough room for the item plus the adhesive strip and flap. A mailer that is too tight strains at the seal, and one that is too large wastes material and shipping space. Sizes run from 9"×12" to 16"×20", and custom sizes are available.

How to choose thickness: Mailers are made in 50 to 60 microns. Soft, light items such as t-shirts, innerwear and accessories usually travel well at the lower end of that range. Heavier or harder items such as footwear, folded denim, books or products with firm corners are better suited to the thicker end, because the film has to resist rubbing and pressure during sorting and handling. A mailer is a cover, not a cushion, so wrap fragile goods in a protective layer first. When you request a quote, tell us the product weight and shipping route, and trial a small batch on your own packing line before ordering in volume.

Disposal and storage: Compostable mailers are designed for industrial composting, where temperature and moisture are controlled. They do not belong in the plastic recycling stream. Our specification states that the mailer returns to soil within 240 days in industrial composting. Remove paper labels and tape where you can, and check which composting facility serves your customers, as access differs from city to city. Store unused mailers in a cool, dry place; shelf life is 12 months from the date of manufacture.

### Courier Bag Sizes Chart: Find the Right Size for Your Product
Page: https://packinclub.com/courier-bag-sizes-chart.html
Published: 15 Oct 2026

Quick answer: Choose a courier bag 1 to 2 inches wider and longer than your folded product; for boxed items, add the box height to both width and length. Many sellers quote size without the flap, which adds about 2 inches, so confirm it. Use 50 microns for light, soft items and 60 microns or more for boxes and heavier parcels.

Key takeaways:
- Pick a courier bag 1 to 2 inches wider and longer than your folded product; for boxed items, add the box height to both width and length.
- Most sellers quote bag size without the flap, which adds roughly 2 inches, so always confirm with your supplier.
- 50 microns suits light, soft products like clothes; 60 microns or more suits boxes, heavier parcels, and long-distance shipping.
- A loose, over-padded bag can push up volumetric weight and increase your shipping cost, even at the same actual weight.
- Certified compostable courier bags come in the same standard sizes as plastic, from 9x12 to 16x20 inches, with custom sizes for bulk orders.

### What Is Compostable Packaging? A Complete Guide
Page: https://packinclub.com/what-is-compostable-packaging.html
Published: 4 Sept 2026

Quick answer: Compostable packaging is made from materials that break down into water, carbon dioxide and nutrient-rich humus under proper composting conditions, instead of fragmenting into microplastics. Common materials include PLA, bagasse, PHA, cellulose and starch blends. A genuine claim in India needs IS 17088 certification and CPCB registration, and it works best when customers have access to real composting.

Key takeaways:
- Compostable packaging fully breaks down into water, CO2, and nutrient-rich humus under proper composting conditions, unlike plastic, which just fragments into microplastics.
- Common materials include PLA, bagasse, PHA, cellulose, and starch blends, each suited to different uses.
- Industrial compostable and home compostable are different, separately timed processes; know which one your packaging is actually certified for.
- A genuine compostable claim requires certification (IS 17088 in India) and CPCB registration, not just the word on a label.
- Compostable packaging works best paired with real composting access; it’s a major improvement over plastic, not a standalone fix on its own.

### Are Compostable Bags Really Eco-Friendly? An Honest Look
Page: https://packinclub.com/are-compostable-bags-really-eco-friendly-an-honest-look.html
Published: 24 Jul 2025

Quick answer: Mostly yes, but with limits. Certified compostable bags solve the persistence and microplastic problem of conventional plastic, yet they are not zero-footprint. Feedstock sourcing, manufacturing energy and access to composting infrastructure still shape the real impact. The most defensible approach is an honest, specific claim such as “certified industrially compostable”, not “100% eco-friendly” or “zero impact”.

Key takeaways:
- Certified compostable packaging genuinely solves the persistence and microplastic problem of conventional plastic, but it isn’t a zero-footprint product.
- Feedstock sourcing, manufacturing energy, and disposal infrastructure access all still shape the real environmental picture.
- Home compostability and industrial compostability are different, separately certified claims, and shouldn’t be used interchangeably in marketing.
- Overclaiming ("100% eco-friendly," "zero impact") creates more brand risk than an honest, specific, qualified claim.
- The most defensible sustainability story acknowledges tradeoffs rather than presenting a single packaging switch as a complete solution.

### How to Spot Greenwashing in Eco-Friendly Packaging: A Buyer's Verification Framework
Page: https://packinclub.com/how-to-spot-greenwashing-in-eco-friendly-packaging.html
Published: 10 Jul 2025

Quick answer: To spot greenwashing, treat “biodegradable”, “compostable” and “recyclable” as three different claims that need different proof. In India, a genuine compostable claim rests on IS/ISO 17088 testing and CPCB certification for a specific product, not a company-wide statement. Ask for the certificate number and test report before you order, because the regulatory and reputational risk lands on the brand owner.

Key takeaways:
- “Biodegradable,” “compostable,” and “recyclable” are three different, non-interchangeable claims with different proof requirements.
- Real compostability claims in India rest on IS/ISO 17088 testing and CPCB certification, tied to a specific product, not a general company statement.
- Certificates need to be checked at the product level, not just the company level. A valid certificate for one product does not cover another.
- Unverified green claims carry regulatory, reputational, and retail-delisting risk that lands on the brand owner, not just the supplier.
- The fastest filter for a genuine supplier is a direct, specific question about test reports and certificate numbers, asked before the order, not after.

### How Long Does Compostable Packaging Take to Decompose?
Page: https://packinclub.com/how-long-does-compostable-packaging-take-to-decompose.html
Published: 16 Jun 2025

Quick answer: Certified compostable plastic under IS/ISO 17088 disintegrates in roughly 12 weeks and fully biodegrades within a maximum of 180 days, but only under industrial composting conditions. Bagasse, paper and plastic film break down at different rates. In a landfill, compostable packaging generally will not decompose on its certified timeframe, so real results depend on reaching a proper composting facility.

Key takeaways:
- Certified compostable plastic under IS/ISO 17088 disintegrates within roughly 12 weeks and fully biodegrades within a maximum of 180 days, under industrial composting conditions specifically.
- Different materials, bagasse, paper, compostable plastic film, decompose at meaningfully different rates, and should not be grouped under one vague timeframe.
- Real-world decomposition speed depends heavily on whether the packaging actually reaches proper industrial composting conditions, not just on the certified lab timeframe.
- Landfill disposal does not replicate composting conditions, and compostable packaging generally will not decompose on its certified timeframe if it ends up there.
- Communicating specific numbers, paired with the correct composting pathway, builds more credibility than a vague "breaks down naturally" claim.

### Home Composting vs Industrial Composting: What You Need to Know
Page: https://packinclub.com/home-composting-vs-industrial-composting-what-you-need-to-know.html
Published: 9 Jun 2025

Quick answer: Home and industrial composting are different processes, with different temperatures, timeframes and certifications. Most standard compostable packaging in India is certified for industrial composting only, under IS/ISO 17088. Home compostability needs a separate, generally stricter certification and should never be assumed. Because industrial facilities are unevenly available across India, match your disposal message to the exact certification your product holds.

Key takeaways:
- Industrial and home composting are different processes with different temperature, consistency, and timeframes, and they require separate certifications.
- Most standard compostable packaging in India is certified for industrial composting only, under IS/ISO 17088.
- Home compostability requires a distinct, generally stricter certification, and shouldn’t be assumed or implied without it.
- Access to industrial composting facilities is uneven across India, which should shape how a brand communicates disposal to customers.
- The safest approach is specifying the exact certification a product holds to your supplier, and matching your customer-facing claim to it precisely.

### Aqueous Coated Paper Cups: Are They Actually Compostable?
Page: https://packinclub.com/aqueous-coated-paper-cups-are-they-actually-compostable.html
Published: 12 May 2025

Quick answer: A paper cup’s compostability depends on its interior lining, not the paper itself. PE-lined cups are not compostable, whatever the marketing says. PLA-lined cups can be compostable, but only with product-specific IS/ISO 17088 certification. “Aqueous coated” is a marketing term, not proof on its own, so ask what the actual liquid barrier is and request the certificate before sourcing.

Key takeaways:
- A paper cup's compostability is determined by its interior lining material, not by the paper itself or by exterior coatings.
- PE-lined cups are not compostable, regardless of aqueous coating or other sustainability language used in marketing.
- PLA-lined cups can be genuinely compostable, but only with product-specific IS/ISO 17088 certification, not by default.
- “Aqueous coated” is a marketing term that needs a follow-up question about the actual liquid barrier, not a standalone compostability claim.
- Verifying lining material and certification before sourcing avoids both a false sustainability claim and a potential compliance gap.

### What Is IS 17088? Compostable Plastic Certification Explained
Page: https://packinclub.com/what-is-is-17088-compostable-plastic-certification-explained.html
Published: 17 Mar 2025

Quick answer: IS 17088 is the Indian standard, based on ISO 17088, behind CPCB certification of compostable plastic sold in India. It tests four things together: disintegration, biodegradation, ecotoxicity and heavy metal content. A certificate covers one specific product and formulation, not a whole company. To verify a claim, ask the supplier for the CPCB registration number and the matching test report.

Key takeaways:
- IS 17088 is the Indian standard, based on ISO 17088, that underpins legal CPCB certification for compostable plastic sold in India.
- Certification tests four separate parameters together: disintegration, biodegradation, ecotoxicity, and heavy metal content.
- A certificate is tied to a specific product and formulation, not a blanket company-wide claim, and needs re-verification when either changes.
- International standards like EN 13432 or ASTM D6400 are legitimate abroad but do not replace IS 17088 and CPCB registration for domestic Indian sale.
- The fastest way to verify a claim is asking directly for the CPCB registration number and the underlying test report, matched to the exact product you are buying.

### India’s Single-Use Plastic Ban: A Practical Compliance Guide for Businesses
Page: https://packinclub.com/india-s-single-use-plastic-ban-a-practical-compliance-guide-for-businesses.html
Published: 3 Mar 2025

Quick answer: India’s plastic ban, carry bag thickness rules and EPR are three separate requirements. A defined list of disposable items has been banned since July 2022; IS 17088 certified compostable versions are exempt. Plastic carry bags need a minimum thickness of 120 microns. EPR makes producers, importers and brand owners register, report and meet recycling targets for packaging outside the ban.

Key takeaways:
- The single-use plastic ban, carry bag thickness rules, and EPR obligations are three separate compliance requirements, not one combined rule.
- A defined list of disposable tableware, straws, certain films and decorative items has been banned since July 2022, with IS 17088 certified compostable versions specifically exempt.
- Plastic carry bags require a minimum thickness of 120 microns, independent of the banned items list.
- EPR applies to plastic packaging not covered by the ban, requiring registration, reporting, and recycling targets for Producers, Importers, and Brand Owners.
- Enforcement has intensified, with more frequent inspections and increasingly digital, traceable compliance checks, making documentation and verification essential rather than optional.

### Compostable vs Biodegradable Packaging: What’s the Real Difference?
Page: https://packinclub.com/compostable-vs-biodegradable-packaging-what-s-the-real-difference.html
Published: 4 Feb 2025

Quick answer: Compostable and biodegradable are not the same. “Biodegradable” is a broad, largely unregulated term with no fixed timeframe, while “compostable” is a certified claim with defined breakdown times and thresholds, such as IS/ISO 17088 in India. Every certified compostable product is biodegradable, but not the reverse. Only certified compostable packaging qualifies for exemptions under India’s single-use plastic ban.

Key takeaways:
- “Biodegradable” is a broad, largely unregulated description; “compostable” is a specific, certifiable claim with defined timeframes and thresholds.
- Every certified compostable product is biodegradable, but not every biodegradable product meets the compostable bar.
- Only certified compostable products, tested under IS/ISO 17088, qualify for exemptions under India’s single-use plastic ban.
- “Biodegradable” alone is easy to claim and hard to verify; treat it as an unverified statement until certification is confirmed.
- Being specific in your own marketing — “certified compostable” rather than just “biodegradable” — is both more defensible and more credible to an informed buyer.
